newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures were steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while calls on feeder cattle ranged mixed, from 0.100 cent per lb lower to 0.100 higher, livestock analysts said.

A better-than-expected tone to cash markets may encourage demand in live cattle futures. Higher cash beef prices posted on Monday were unexpected and could keep packer interest for cattle somewhat better than projected earlier in the month, analysts said.
Boxed beef prices had been expected to ease seasonally now that retailer buying for Independence Day featuring is largely complete.
Sources said the majority of beef sold the remainder of the summer likely would be ground beef rather than cuts such as steaks and roasts.
USDA quoted closing boxed beef cut-out values on Monday up $0.24 to $0.53 per cwt.

An expected reversal in corn futures to possibly higher prices and a break in the latest CME feeder cattle index were expected to weigh on feeder cattle futures. However, seasonal considerations remain pointing upward which could spark mixed trade. In 14 of the last 15 years, feeder cattle futures have trended higher between late June and early August, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index fell $0.45 to $77.56 per cwt.
